The thing is that trees actually seed rain clouds. That's the "chicken and egg" problem with desertification. The only way to stop it is to seed more rain, and the only way to do that in large quantities is to have trees. Other plants will have some effect, but deep-rooted trees simply pull up more moisture from the ground than do other plants (as far as I'm aware).

It is entirely possible that part of the reason for enhanced desertification is excessive grazing, and that's not about individuals being stupid. In fact it's entirely within your self interest in the short term to have the largest herd sizes possible to maximize your profitability, and so there's no incentive to encourage long-term growth of trees as the herds eat the young sprouts. Then there's wood cut for fire that doesn't regrow due to the grazing and... you get the idea. It's basically "The Tragedy of the Commons" on a mass scale, and before humans domesticated animals large herds of herbivores were already responsible for much of the expansion.

So if you want to fix this problem then what is needed is for large-scale animal herding to become obsolete. Or very intensive well enforced regulations to require planting and expansion of forests in the region. However, since a lot of these people are isolated and essentially tenant farmers or sharecroppers, there's no incentive on the ground for any of them to improve their surroundings. The blight of sharecropping is directly responsible for the dust bowl, too, because sharecroppers had no incentive to maintain land they would never be able to own.
